Prerequisite: Log sources (FortiGates, other Fortinet devices, and syslog devices) set to send logs to the FortiAnalyzer, registered, and authorized
What it enables: Log collection, per-device quotas, rate limits, integrity checks, and backups, no-logging detection, and the features built on one product's logs (for example FortiMail, FortiWeb, FortiDeceptor, FortiSandbox, FortiNDR, or FortiEDR logs)
How to put it in place: On each device, send logs to the FortiAnalyzer's address; then authorize the device in GUI: Device Manager, and check it with diagnose dvm device list
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system admin setting (unreg_dev_opt) and diagnose dvm device list; Chapter 12 rows *Device registration and authorization* and *Security Fabric authorization*

Prerequisite: ADOMs enabled and created, with the devices and administrators assigned to them
What it enables: Per-ADOM disk quotas, data policies, log rates, time zones, and administrator profiles, ADOM assignment of administrators, Fabric ADOMs, and EMS multitenancy
How to put it in place: config system global; set adom-status enable; end, then create the ADOMs in the GUI and assign administrators with config system admin user; edit <ADMIN>; set adom <ADOM>; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, "Administrative Domains" ("Configuring ADOMs": the feature must first be enabled, ADOMs created, and administrators assigned) and config system global (adom-status)

Prerequisite: Log storage sized for the retention period: disks on a hardware unit, or virtual disks on a FortiAnalyzer-VM, within the license's storage limits
What it enables: Disk quotas, the data policy (retention), and disk-full alerting with room to store logs for the required period
How to put it in place: Hardware: a model with enough disk capacity. VM: add a virtual disk, then execute lvm extend, and check with execute lvm info
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, execute lvm (FortiAnalyzer VM models only); FortiAnalyzer 7.2 New Features Guide, "FortiAnalyzer-VM has been added to the Flex-VM offering" (the license sets the daily storage and number of ADOMs)

Prerequisite: Reachable RADIUS, TACACS+, or LDAP servers, each with a unique shared secret or bind account, and administrator accounts that use them
What it enables: Remote administrator authentication, so the authentication server enforces password, inactivity, and lockout rules
How to put it in place: An organization RADIUS, TACACS+, or LDAP service, then config system admin radius; edit <RADIUS>; set server <RADIUS_IP>; set secret <SECRET>; end and config system admin user; edit <ADMIN>; set user_type radius; set radius_server <RADIUS>; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system admin radius, config system admin tacacs, config system admin ldap, and config system admin user (user_type, radius_server, tacacs-plus-server, ldap-server); Chapter 12 rows *RADIUS administrator authentication*, *TACACS+ administrator authentication*, and *LDAP administrator authentication*

Prerequisite: A SAML identity provider with the FortiAnalyzer registered as a service provider, and the IdP certificate on the FortiAnalyzer
What it enables: SAML single sign-on for administrators, with signed assertions and requests and SHA-256 or SHA-512 signatures
How to put it in place: An organization SAML IdP, then config system saml; set status enable; set role SP; set idp-entity-id <IDP_ENTITY_ID>; set idp-single-sign-on-url <IDP_SSO_URL>; set idp-cert <IDP_CERT>; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system saml; Chapter 12 rows *SAML SSO wildcard admin user to match all users on IdP server*, *SAML assertions and SAML requests can be now signed to better support third-party IdPs*, and *SAML SSO supports SHA-256 and SHA-512 for both IdP and SP*

Prerequisite: PKI: the DoD CA certificates and CRLs on the FortiAnalyzer, a reachable CRL distribution point, and certificates from that PKI for administrators and log sources
What it enables: PKI (certificate) administrator login, two-factor authentication (available only for PKI administrators), LDAPS server validation, and syslog client certificate authentication
How to put it in place: config system certificate ca; edit <DOD_CA>; set ca <CA_CERTIFICATE>; end and config system certificate crl; edit <DOD_CRL>; set http-url <CRL_URL>; end, with certificates issued to the administrators and the syslog log sources
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system certificate ca, config system certificate crl, config system admin user (user_type pki-auth, ca; two-factor-auth is available when a PKI administrator account is configured), and config system log settings (client-cert-auth); Chapter 12 rows *PKI (certificate) administrator authentication* and *CA certificates and CRLs*

Prerequisite: FortiToken Cloud with a token for each administrator
What it enables: Two-factor authentication for administrators (FortiToken Cloud email, mobile, or SMS)
How to put it in place: FortiToken Cloud, then config system admin user; edit <ADMIN>; set two-factor-auth ftc-ftm; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system admin user (two-factor-auth); Chapter 12 row *Two-factor authentication (FortiToken Cloud)*

Prerequisite: A reachable SMTP server (with STARTTLS and an account if it requires authentication)
What it enables: Alert email to the ISSO and administrators: disk-full, no-logging, and system alerts, and event handler and scheduled notifications
How to put it in place: An organization mail server, then config system mail; edit <SMTP>; set server <SMTP_IP>; set secure-option starttls; set auth enable; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system mail and config system alert-event; Chapter 12 row *Alert email (SMTP)*

Prerequisite: SNMPv3 manager configured with the same user, authentication, and privacy settings
What it enables: SNMPv3 queries and notifications with SHA-2 authentication and AES privacy
How to put it in place: The organization network management system, then config system snmp user; edit <USER>; set notify-hosts <NMS_IP>; set queries enable; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system snmp user; Chapter 12 row *SNMPv3*

Prerequisite: Authoritative NTP servers and their authentication keys
What it enables: Synchronized, authenticated time for the FortiAnalyzer's own records and for log receipt time stamps
How to put it in place: Organization NTP servers, then config system ntp; config ntpserver; edit 1; set server <NTP_IP>; set authentication enable; set key-type sha256; set key-id <ID>; set key <KEY>; end; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system ntp; Chapter 12 rows *NTP server* and *FortiAnalyzer supports NTPv4 with SHA-256 encryption*

Prerequisite: A remote syslog server or SIEM that accepts reliable (TCP) syslog with TLS
What it enables: Off-loading the FortiAnalyzer's own event logs, and forwarding collected logs in real time to a different system
How to put it in place: An organization syslog server or SIEM, then config system syslog; edit <SYSLOG>; set ip <SYSLOG_IP>; set reliable enable; set secure-connection enable; end for the FortiAnalyzer's own logs, or config system log-forward; edit 1; set mode forwarding; set server-addr <SIEM_IP>; end for collected logs
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system syslog and config system log-forward; Chapter 12 rows *Sending FortiAnalyzer event logs to a syslog server* and *Log forwarding to syslog, CEF, or another FortiAnalyzer*

Prerequisite: Another FortiAnalyzer: the analyzer that receives aggregated logs, or the server that log fetching pulls from
What it enables: Log aggregation from a collector to an analyzer, and log fetching between FortiAnalyzer units
How to put it in place: On the analyzer, config system log-forward-service; set accept-aggregation enable; end; for log fetching, the other unit is the fetch server (config system log-fetch server-setting)
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system log-forward-service (accept-aggregation), config system log-fetch server-setting, and config system log-fetch client-profile; Chapter 12 rows *Log aggregation (collector to analyzer)* and *Log fetching between FortiAnalyzer units*

Prerequisite: An SFTP server and account for backups and firmware images
What it enables: Log and configuration backups to another system, the backup before an upgrade, and loading firmware from the CLI
How to put it in place: An organization SFTP server; the backup runs execute backup all-settings sftp <SERVER_IP> <FILE> <USER> <PASSWORD>
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, execute backup, execute restore image, and config system backup all-settings; Chapter 12 rows *Log backup to another system*, *Configuration backup*, and *Firmware upgrade*

Prerequisite: Console access to the FortiAnalyzer (serial console, or the hypervisor console of a VM)
What it enables: Enabling FIPS-CC mode, which is available only from the console
How to put it in place: A console connection, then config system fips; set status enable; end
Source: FortiAnalyzer 8.0.0 CLI Reference, config system fips (the enable option is available only through the console); Chapter 12 row *FIPS-CC mode*

Prerequisite: A valid FortiCare support contract: the Firmware & General Updates entitlement, and FortiCare Premium or Elite
What it enables: Upgrades to a higher major or minor release, and object updates from FortiGuard (FortiGate metadata, Internet Service Database, GeoIP, safeguarding)
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the contract in FortiCloud; check with diagnose fmupdate dbcontract and diagnose license list
Source: FortiAnalyzer 7.4 New Features Guide, "Prevent FortiAnalyzers with an expired support contract from upgrading to a major or minor firmware release"; FortiAnalyzer 8.0 New Features Guide, "FortiCare Elite or FortiCare Premium required to download FortiGuard objects"

What it enables: IOC detection (compromised hosts) and the charts that depend on it
How to put it in place: Purchase and register the license; check with diagnose license list or GUI: Dashboards > Status > License Information
Source: FortiAnalyzer 7.0 New Features Guide, "DNS security report 7.0.3" (without IOC, the charts show "No license for the Indicators of Compromise (IOC) service")
